clue.text: Lavish friends returned to London, say

indicators.note: returned means the word for friends comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: pals are friends
one goes up to London, the capital, as to any important centre

explanation.surface: Generous companions come back to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PALS into SLAP; in British usage you travel 'up' to London from anywhere, so 'to London' gives UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, lavishly generous feast, in informal British usage.

clue.text: Examine ring, certainly acceptable to sweetheart

indicators.note: acceptable to means the other pieces are received into the word for sweetheart

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart
O is ring-shaped
OK means certainly, all right

explanation.surface: Inspect an engagement ring to make sure the fiancée will like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acceptable to' puts O and OK inside LOVER, after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over something is to inspect or check it briefly.

clue.text: You need to secure right sort of oven for this

definitions.text: You need to secure right sort of oven for this

parts.note: to pot is to secure or win, as one pots a prize
an oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: get the proper kind of oven for this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, familiar in Kent. The whole clue also describes a dish that needs the right oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot roast is a joint of meat braised slowly in a covered pot.

clue.text: Performer of the Dada school?

parts.note: read Dada as a child's word for father, i.e. pop, and performer as artist: an entertainer of the 'pop' school, rather than a Dadaist painter

explanation.surface: A member of the early 20th-century anti-art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Dada, the art movement, is also baby talk for father, which is Pop.
explanation.definitionFit: Warhol or Lichtenstein made art from comics and adverts, the movement that followed Dada's spirit.

clue.text: In states on both coasts, parties needed drink

parts.note: Cal. is California, a state on the Pacific coast
VA is Virginia, a state on the Atlantic coast
dos are parties, informal celebrations

explanation.surface: Party-goers across America from east to west needed something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: One state from each US coast is wanted: CAL (California, west) and VA (Virginia, east); 'In' and 'needed' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is an apple brandy from Normandy, a spirit one drinks.

clue.text: GP has to locate it for special treatment?

definitions.text: GP has to locate it for special treatment?

indicators.note: giving the words special treatment means working them over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A family doctor must find somewhere for patients needing particular care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for special treatment' rearranges all fifteen letters of GP HAS TO LOCATE IT, and the whole clue describes where a GP sends patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural hospital, often staffed by local general practitioners, serving a country district.

clue.text: I turn green, initially, in this uncomfortable condition

indicators.note: initially says the word for green comes first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
taken as written
a go is a turn, as in your go

explanation.surface: Someone feeling sick describes going green in a dizzy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' moves VERT (heraldic green) to the front, before I and GO; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of dizziness, often with nausea, from looking down from heights.

clue.text: The lower classes intended to show bold resistance

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British socio-economic classification
one's intended is one's fiancé

explanation.surface: The working classes meant to stand up for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades people A, B, C1, C2, D and E; D and E are the lowest. 'intended' is a noun here, a husband-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open, bold refusal to obey or submit.

clue.text: A couple of blue shades used for window

parts.note: sky is a shade of blue, as in sky blue
light is a shade of blue, as in light blue

explanation.surface: Two blue window blinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shades' suggests blinds; it means colours: sky blue and light blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A skylight is a window set into a roof or ceiling.

clue.text: Affectionate feeling it's not hard to notice

parts.note: something not hard is soft
to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: A fondness that is easy to recognise.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a soft spot for someone is a fondness or tender liking for them.

clue.text: It's designed to be attractive, on the surface

definitions.text: It's designed to be attractive, on the surface

parts.words: It's designed to be attractive, on the surface
parts.note: read as a fishing lure: an angler's bait made to tempt trout while floating on the water, not something merely superficially pretty

explanation.surface: Something whose charm is only skin-deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the surface' seems to mean superficially; in fly fishing a dry fly floats on the water's surface to attract fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers tie this lure to float atop the water and entice rising trout.

clue.text: Exclusive neighbourhood

parts.note: read not as a posh district but as a district that excludes people, one where outsiders dare not enter

explanation.surface: A select, upmarket part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' suggests upmarket; here it means literally keeping people out.
explanation.definitionFit: A district that is dangerous or forbidden to enter is one people are barred from.

clue.text: Eastern festival one Western artist has captured

indicators.note: has captured means the painter's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist artist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter has taken a single Westerner captive at an Oriental celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has captured' puts I and W inside DALI, after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, celebrated in India and across South Asia.

clue.text: Weapon landed the wrong way in fight

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word for landed is read backwards

parts.note: a bird lit, or landed, on a branch

explanation.surface: A weapon that came down awkwardly during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns LIT into TIL, and 'in' places TIL inside SET-TO, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender blade.

clue.text: Part of year in which to cut trees, perhaps

parts.note: to trim is to cut

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word trees might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A season in which to prune woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TREES into ESTER after TRIM; 'in which to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a third of the academic year, a term.

clue.text: Badly behaved child, aberrant at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every other letter of the word aberrant, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster who misbehaves now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'aberrant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a spoilt or unruly youngster.

clue.text: Stop Daily Telegraph's leader showing statistical graph

parts.note: to bar is to stop or prevent
a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in by day, also called a char

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the word Telegraph

explanation.surface: A call to ban the newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Telegraph' looks like the newspaper; split it. A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaner, also called a CHAR, and 'Telegraph's leader' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart displays quantities as columns of different heights, a kind of diagram for data.

clue.text: Unfortunate occurrence of stress I had taken to heart

indicators.note: taken to heart means the contracted pronoun-and-verb goes into the middle of the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is stress on a syllable
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A mishap caused by stress that I took to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to heart' places ID in the middle of ACCENT, after ACC.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is a mishap, something happening unexpectedly and unluckily.

clue.text: Final with spell of extra time

definitions.text: Final with spell of extra time

parts.words: Final with spell of extra time
parts.note: read 'time' as its abbreviation T: a word for final, as in a final total after deductions, spelt with an extra T on the end

explanation.surface: A cup final that went into extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra time' looks like football; T is the standard abbreviation for time, and the answer is the word for final (after deductions) spelt with one more T.
explanation.definitionFit: The variant spelling with a doubled T means remaining after all deductions, as a final figure does.

clue.text: Reporter takes novel by Irish author to king

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright
K is the abbreviation for king, in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A journalist brings a book by an Irish writer to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning new. 'takes' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A newshawk is a slangy American term for an energetic news reporter.

clue.text: Chicken and duck on American island to the North

indicators.note: to the North, in a down clue, means the island's name sits above the other pieces

parts.note: Timor is an island in Southeast Asia
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
US is short for American, United States

explanation.surface: A recipe of poultry and duck on an island in the north of America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to the North' puts TIMOR on top; O 'on' US stacks the duck above US.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken in slang means cowardly, and timorous means fearful or timid.

clue.text: A form of protein that has many medical applications

definitions.text: A form of protein that has many medical applications

indicators.note: a form of something is a reshaped version of it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A protein variant widely used in medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then an anagram of PROTEIN (signalled by 'form of') gives TROPINE. Strictly the drug is an alkaloid, not a protein, so the whole clue is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a drug from deadly nightshade used to dilate pupils and treat a slow heartbeat, among many uses.

clue.text: Zola, for example, presenting a small volume to employer

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetre, is a small measure of volume
a user employs something, so is its employer

explanation.surface: The French novelist offering a slim book to his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola's famous open letter 'J'accuse' charged the French army in the Dreyfus affair. 'volume' looks like a book; it is a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola publicly charged officials with wrongdoing, making him an accuser, one who lays charges.

clue.text: Tightly hold line in firm grip

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for line is placed inside the word for a firm grip

parts.note: a cinch is a firm grip, also a saddle girth

explanation.surface: Hold a rope securely in your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside CINCH, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch is to grip someone tightly, as boxers do in close embrace.

clue.text: Urge to fight for journalists' position

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
to box is to fight with the fists

explanation.surface: Encouraging reporters to come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: The press box is the area at a sports ground reserved for reporters.

clue.text: Distorted images that would upset old-timers

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: the thing that would offend elderly people

indicators.note: distorted means the letters of the word images are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Warped pictures that would trouble older people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distorted' rearranges IMAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination against people because of their age, which the elderly resent.

clue.text: Animal caught in intricate trap, oddly

indicators.note: caught in means the letters lie captured inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A creature snared in an elaborate trap in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across intricaTE TRAP ODdly; 'oddly' is not an odd-letters signal here but part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrapod is any four-limbed vertebrate, so an animal.

clue.text: A learning experience, getting out unfortunately in test

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: unfortunately means the word out ends up in a bad, jumbled state

explanation.surface: Failing an exam is a lesson in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns OUT into UTO, and 'in' puts UTO inside TRIAL after its T; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session with a tutor, a period of instruction.

clue.text: Jaunty and dissolute

definitions.meaning: jaunty, as a hat worn at a dashing, cocky angle
dissolute, as a debauched man about town

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stylishly devil-may-care and morally loose, like a libertine.
